sec: Bone formation hypotheses and ALP · p865

items.q: The bone mineral is formed as ___ from the amorphous calcium phosphate precursor.
items.exp: Amorphous calcium phosphate (precursor) → calcium hydroxy apatite (bone). (Book p865)

items.q: In the OLD hypothesis, mineralisation at the metaphyseal end is driven by which enzymes?
items.exp: Old hypothesis: osteoblast lays matrix (type I collagen) then mineralisation by ALP, annexin, 5'-nucleotidase; osteoblast → osteocyte. (Book p865)
ALP hydrolyses inhibitors of mineralisation; ↑ mineralisation → ↑ ALP. (Book p865)

items.q: ‘Serum ALP is NOT raised in multiple myeloma because mineralisation is decreased there.’
opts: False — ALP is high in myeloma
items.exp: ALP is not ↑ in multiple myeloma as mineralisation is ↓. (Book p865)

items.q: The sources of ALP listed are:
items.exp: Sources of ALP: bone, kidney, placenta. (Book p865)

items.q: The NEW hypothesis of bone formation states that:
opts: Osteoblast converts to osteocyte, and the osteocyte lays down matrix and mineralises it
items.exp: New hypothesis: osteoblast → osteocyte; osteocyte lays down matrix → mineralisation (bone added outside-to-inside by osteocytes). (Book p865)

items.q: Which enzyme has ONLY a liver source and helps confirm the hepatic origin of a raised ALP?
items.exp: GGT is only liver source and confirms hepatic origin of ↑ALP; ALP and 5'-nucleotidase are not specific (other sources). (Book p865)

items.q: Which is NOT a cholestatic liver enzyme in the note?
items.exp: Cholestatic liver enzymes: ALP, 5'-nucleotidase (not specific), GGT (liver-only) — not ALT. (Book p865)
